newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin Source sees Svyazinv sale delay. [CORRECTED 13:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Kremlin Source sees Svyazinv sale delay. [CORRECTED 13:50 GMT]

text.p: A draft decree authorising the privatisation and sale of 49 percent of Russian telecom holding company AO Svyazinvest may be held up on legal grounds by the presidential administration, a Kremlin source said on Thursday. (Corrects to make clear decree may be held up, not has been held up.)
"Essentially the scheme does not meet the realities of legislation," the source told Reuters without giving details.
The delay will also hold up the planned transfer of the government's 38 percent stake in long-distance operator Rostelekom to Svyazinvest.

Communications Minister Vladimir Bulgak said in January that President Boris Yeltsin would probably sign a decree in February authorising sales this year of 25 percent of Svyazinvest to foreign investors and 24 percent to Russian investors.
Bulgak said Russia would seek portfolio investors rather than strategic investors.

Earlier this month Svyazinvest chief executive Nail Ismailov said the decree would also cover the transfer of the Rostelekom stake, which amounts to 51 percent of the voting shares, and stakes in some other companies, including 38 percent of the Tsentralny Telegraf communications company.
Svyazinvest has controlling packets in 85 regional telecommunications companies.
